claims.text: Nearly equiatomic five-transition-metal HEA nanoparticles can initially possess disordered FCC or BCC solid-solution structures.
HEA nanoparticles possess a high surface-to-volume ratio.
High configurational entropy can stabilize multielement solid solutions and suppress intermetallic formation in bulk HEAs.
Low or sluggish atomic diffusion kinetically restrains precipitation and contributes to HEA stability.
Severe lattice distortion is responsible for sluggish diffusion in bulk HEAs.
Surface-induced severe lattice distortion compromises the thermal stability of five-metal HEA nanoparticles.
The high fraction of surface atoms reduces the effective configurational entropy of HEA nanoparticles.
Surface-induced distortion and entropy reduction alter local chemical ordering and lower the energy barrier for phase separation.
Nanoparticle surfaces provide enhanced diffusion pathways that negate the sluggish-diffusion effect.
Negating sluggish diffusion permits rapid atomic rearrangement and precipitation, ordering, phase separation, or amorphization.
Ordered-phase formation or phase separation reduces the configurational entropy of an HEA.
Phase separation in these nanoparticles is driven by reduction of surface energy rather than bulk thermodynamic instability.
Thermal stability varies non-monotonically with nanoparticle size.
Particles smaller than 20 nm rapidly phase-separate or order at temperatures where bulk counterparts remain stable.
Loss of the single-phase solid solution will degrade mechanical properties, including the strength-ductility combination.
Bulk equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi maintains a single-phase solid solution and sluggish diffusion to high temperatures because of configurational entropy and lattice distortion.
Bulk equiatomic NbTaTiV maintains single-phase stability and sluggish diffusion to high temperatures.
Above approximately 100 nm, bulk thermodynamics dominates nanoparticle behavior and the proposed instability mechanism fails.
Sufficiently high cohesive energy can keep surface diffusion negligible even at elevated temperature.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations affect the temperature-dependent phase stability of CoCrFeMnNi, but their role in stabilizing FCC nanoparticles is not quantified.

contradictions.description: Severe lattice distortion is invoked as the bulk origin of sluggish diffusion, but surface-induced severe lattice distortion is also said to lower the barrier for phase separation and enhance rearrangement. The hypothesis does not distinguish the forms of distortion or explain why their kinetic effects are opposite.
